name: Beef Borsch with Sour Cream
description: A hearty beet-based soup with shredded beef, vegetables, and a dollop of sour cream on top.
recipeIngredient: 2 Tbsp snipped fresh dill or 2 tsp dried dill weed

recipeInstructions.text: Day before serving, place beef, marrow bone, 2 quarts water, and 1 Tbsp salt in a deep 8-quart kettle. Cover and bring to boiling, then reduce heat and simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
Add tomatoes, quartered onion, celery, parsley, black pepper, and bay leaf. Simmer, covered, for 2 hours longer.
Remove from heat. Lift out beef and set aside. Remove marrow bone and discard. Strain soup and skim off fat (you should have 9 cups liquid).

Return soup and beef to kettle. Add beets, cabbage, carrots, chopped onion, dill, vinegar, sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to boiling, then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until beef and vegetables are tender.
Cool for 20 minutes, then refrigerate overnight.
The next day, remove beef from soup and cut into cubes. Return to soup and heat gently to boiling.
Pour into soup tureen. Top each serving with a spoonful of sour cream and garnish with snipped dill.

keywords: beef borsch, sour cream, beet soup, Eastern European soup

_similar.name: Meat Balls and Sour And Sweet Sauce
_similar.description: A classic meatball recipe served in a tangy sweet and sour sauce, perfect for serving over meatballs, chicken, or pork chops.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp onion flakes or 1 tsp real onion

recipeInstructions.text: Mix all ingredients together and form into 1½ inch balls.
Bake in an ungreased oblong pan for 20 to 25 minutes at 400°F.
Remove from oven and drain grease.
Place meatballs in a large casserole.
Pour sweet and sour sauce over the top and return to oven for 10 minutes or until hot.
To make the sauce, mix all ingredients together in a saucepan and stir while bringing to a boil until thickened.

_similar.name: Creamy Beef and Potato Bake
_similar.description: A layered casserole featuring ground beef, potatoes, zucchini, and a creamy cheddar sauce.
recipeIngredient: ½ cup prepared tomato pasta sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F to 375°F.
In a skillet, melt 2 tablespoons butter and oil over medium-low heat. Add potatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add zucchini, salt, and pepper to the skillet. Cook until zucchini is tender.
Spoon the vegetable mixture into a 13x9 inch baking dish. Set aside.
In the same skillet, cook onion and Italian seasoning until onion is tender.
Add ground beef to the skillet and cook until it loses its pink color. Stir in tomato sauce and ½ cup milk.
Spoon the meat mixture over the vegetable layer in the baking dish.
Melt remaining butter in the skillet, stir in flour, and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in remaining milk. Cook and stir until the sauce thickens.
Stir in cheddar cheese until melted. Pour the sauce over the meat layer.
Bake at 350°F for 20 to 25 minutes.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

_similar.keywords: beef casserole, potato bake, creamy sauce

_similar.name: Sweet & Sour Meatballs
_similar.description: A hearty meatball dish smothered in a rich sweet and sour pineapple sauce, baked to perfection.
recipeIngredient: For the sauce: ½ cup brown sugar, ½ cup vinegar, 19 oz pineapple tidbits (undrained), ½ tsp salt, 1 Tbsp cornstarch

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together ground beef, onion, cracker crumbs, garlic, pepper, egg, and milk. Chill until firm.
Shape into evenly sized meatballs and place on a greased broiler pan.
Broil to brown on all sides, watching carefully.
Place meatballs in a casserole dish.
To make the sauce, combine brown sugar, salt, and cornstarch. Gradually stir in vinegar and soya sauce. Add pineapple tidbits and bring to a boil until thickened and clear.
Pour the sauce over the meatballs and bake in the oven at 350°F for 1 hour.

_similar.keywords: sweet and sour meatballs, baked meatballs, pineapple sauce
